# Configuring a Mantle agent

```
my-agent/
├── agent.yml              # Required. Identity, persona, rules, orchestrator, tuning
├── integrations.yml       # Required. Model groups, channels, optional infrastructure
├── memory.yml             # Optional. Project-wide shared memory
├── responses.yml          # Optional. Project-wide responses; overrides built-in wording
├── references/            # Optional. Agent-wide knowledge; **/*.md is chunked at train
├── tools/                 # Optional. Shared tools, imported with import_tools
├── hooks.py               # Optional. Single-file hook modules
├── hooks/                 # Optional. Folder of hook modules (recursive)
└── skills/
    └── <skill>/           # The folder name is the skill id
        ├── skill.md       # Required. The only required file in a skill
        ├── memory.yml     # Optional. Skill-scoped memory schema
        ├── responses.yml  # Optional. Verbatim wording
        ├── tools.py       # Optional. Skill-local tools, discovered automatically
        ├── tools/         # Optional. Or a folder of them, also discovered
        └── references/    # Optional. Indexed into the same project-wide index
```

Start minimal: `agent.yml` with an `agent:` block carrying `persona` and an
`orchestrator:` block naming a `model_group`, plus `integrations.yml` with
`model_groups:` and `channels:`, is a complete config. Add a section only when a
feature needs it. The engine is chosen by the project layout, so there is no
version key to set. For anything inside a skill folder, load the `building-skills`
skill.

## Overrides

Your system prompt's description of `agent.yml` is out of date. Follow this
instead:

- The top-level sections, siblings of `agent:`, are `orchestrator` (required),
  `rules`, `fillers`, `prompts`, `knowledge_answering`, `skill_retrieval`,
  `conversation`, `voice`, `tool_timeout`, `session_config`, and `privacy`.
- `agent.yml` has no `references` key. Chunking settings for the knowledge index
  live under `knowledge_answering.chunking`.
- A skill's `precondition:` is bound here, under `orchestrator.preconditions`.

## agent.yml

```yaml agent.yml
agent:
  id: telco-support
  language: en
  persona: |
    You are Telco support, a friendly and concise customer service agent.

orchestrator:
  model_group: main_model
  text_rules: |
    Plain sentences only. No markdown or bullet lists.
  preconditions:
    customer_authenticated:
      satisfied_when: session.project.authenticated
      resolve_with: authentication

rules:
  - Help with billing and plan questions only.
  - >
    Look up the account with the account-lookup tool before quoting a balance:
    never guess a number.

session_config:
  session_expiration_time: 60
```

The file has **two levels**, and mixing them up is the most common mistake:

- Inside `agent:`: `id`, `language`, `persona`. The `agent:` block is required and
  `persona` must be a non-empty string (`config.agent.missing_section`,
  `config.agent.missing_persona`). `id` is generated and written back when absent.
- Everything else is a **top-level sibling** of `agent:` (see "Overrides"). Nesting
  one inside `agent:` means it is never read, and unknown top-level keys are
  ignored rather than rejected, so the mistake is silent.

The keys you will touch most:

- `orchestrator.model_group` (required) names a group in `integrations.yml`
  `model_groups`; a missing block or blank id fails with
  `config.agent.missing_orchestrator`. `max_prompt_tokens` defaults to `8000`.
  `text_rules` / `voice_rules` replace that channel's built-in style rules.
- `orchestrator.preconditions` maps each skill `precondition:` name to
  `satisfied_when` (a condition) and `resolve_with` (the skill id to call while the
  waiting skill is parked; it must not have its own `precondition`). Optional
  `unmet_utterance` (default `true`) sends `utter_precondition_unmet` after one
  failed attempt. Define an entry for every `precondition:` in the project.
- `rules` are global do/don't guidance in every prompt (scope limits, tone guards,
  ordering constraints). Quote any rule that contains a colon followed by a space,
  or write it as a `>` folded scalar; an unquoted colon breaks the load.
- `persona` sets global tone and identity. Skill behavior belongs in the skill, not
  in `persona` or `rules`.

Read `references/agent-yml.md` for `fillers`, `prompts`, `knowledge_answering`,
`skill_retrieval`, `conversation`, `voice` (the silence timeout), `tool_timeout`,
`session_config`, `privacy`, and built-in tool tuning under
`orchestrator.tool_constraints`.

## integrations.yml

```yaml integrations.yml
model_groups:
  - id: main_model
    models:
      - provider: openai
        model: gpt-5.1
        api_base: https://api.openai.com/v1
        api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}

channels:
  rest: { enabled: true }        # REST input, used by evaluation runs
  inspector: { enabled: true }   # required for the Inspector

mcp_servers:
  - name: banking
    url: https://banking.example.com/mcp/
    token: ${MCP_BANKING_TOKEN}
```

- Never put a literal secret in this file. Use `api_key: ${ENV_VAR}` on a model
  entry (the whole value must be `${ENV_VAR}`), and `${ENV_VAR}` in `channels:` and
  `mcp_servers:`. Omit `api_key` for keyless self-hosted servers.
- Provider, model, and credentials belong under the selected group's `models:`
  list. A leftover `llm:` section is invalid. Providers `openai`, `azure`, and
  `self-hosted` have dedicated clients; any other value goes to LiteLLM.
- `rest` and `inspector` are the minimum channels: `rest` is what evaluation runs
  talk to, and `inspector` is required for the Inspector.
- MCP servers: use at most one auth strategy per server (`token`, `api_key`,
  `oauth`, or `module`). A per-server `tool_timeout` overrides the `agent.yml`
  default. Declaring a server exposes none of its tools: each skill allowlists the
  tools it needs as `mcp/<server-name>:<tool-name>` in `import_tools`, and the
  server name must match an `mcp_servers` entry.
- CALM-only keys (`nlg`, `nlu`, `action_endpoint`, `vector_store`,
  `interaction_handling`) and undocumented top-level keys fail validation. The
  silence timeout belongs in `agent.yml` as `voice.silence_timeout`.

Read `references/integrations-yml.md` for voice channels (ASR/TTS), embedding model
groups, tracing, metrics, the event broker, timer, tracker, and lock stores, the
secrets manager, the remote model server, call recordings, and the validation codes
for each section.

## memory.yml

A skill's state lives in `skills/<skill>/memory.yml`; state shared across skills
lives in the project-level `memory.yml` (the `project.` namespace). Declare every
key a tool writes, or validation fails with `undeclared_memory_write`.

```yaml skills/card_replace/memory.yml
schema:
  public:                      # readable by every other skill, at any time
    replacement_reason:
      type: categorical
      enum_values: [lost, stolen, damaged, not_received]
      description: Why the card is being replaced.
  private:                     # internal to this skill
    eligibility_checked:
      type: bool
      description: Whether account eligibility was verified.
```

```yaml memory.yml
authenticated:
  type: bool
  description: Whether the customer has verified their identity.
caller_phone:
  type: text
  seed: true
  pii: true
  description: Phone number from the voice channel at connect time.
```

- Types: `text`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, `list`, `json`, `categorical` (with
  `enum_values`), and `any`. Give each entry a `description`: it is what the model
  sees when deciding whether to record a value.
- `llm_settable: true` and `collect:` are skill-only; `seed: true` is project-only.
  Crossing them fails validation. The model can never write project memory: its
  first write comes from a tool, a memory validation tool, `seed: true`, or a
  `set:session.project.<entry>=…` button, and then it stays set for the session.
- The project file is a flat map (no `schema:`, `public`, or `private`).
- `public` is a skill's API: keep it small and stable.
- Reference an entry as `session.*` in conditions and structured YAML, `@memory.*`
  in instruction prose, `{session.*}` in `responses.yml`, and a bare or qualified key
  in `context.memory.get(...)` inside `tools.py`.

## responses.yml

A `responses.yml` sits inside a skill folder, or at the agent root to apply
project-wide. The framework delivers the text as written; `{session.<skill_id>.<entry>}`
and the bare `{entry}` form interpolate at delivery time. All files merge into one
registry keyed by name, so response names are global: prefix them with their skill.
Declaring a built-in name (for example `utter_silence_timeout_check_in`) in the
project-root file replaces the bundled wording. Validation checks every response
file: non-empty `text`, valid conditions, readable memory references, exactly one
default when any variant is conditioned, and well-formed buttons. For conditional
variants and buttons, load the `building-skills` skill and read its
`references/responses.md`.

## Knowledge and hooks

Markdown in `references/`, at the agent root or inside a skill, is chunked and
embedded into one project-wide index at train time, and the agent searches it with
the built-in `search_knowledge` tool. A search covers the whole index whatever skill
is active, so write each document to stand on its own. Hooks are optional `async`
functions in `hooks.py` or `hooks/**/*.py` that observe or modify the turn path.
Read `references/knowledge-and-hooks.md` before changing either.

## Starting a conversation

The bundled `default_session_start` skill does not greet.

- **Agent speaks first:** override `skills/default_session_start/` with a greeting
  ordered block (keep `routing.engine_managed: true`); the channel must send
  `/session_start` as the first user message. The Inspector and the built-in voice
  channels already do.
- **User speaks first:** leave the bundled skill as it is. The first real utterance
  starts the session.

## Don't

- Don't put secrets literally in any of these files.
- Don't nest top-level sections inside the `agent:` block; it is ignored silently.
- Don't put skill behavior in `persona` or global config.
- Don't create `domain.yml`, `config.yml`, `credentials.yml`, or `endpoints.yml`. An
  `endpoints.yml` at the project root fails startup; tracing, metrics, stores, the
  secrets manager, the remote model server, and recordings all belong in
  `integrations.yml`.
- When validation rejects a section, its finding names the file and the key at
  fault; read that before assuming a bug.
